title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
content_md: GL.iNet has confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices, with some affected users reporting backdoors and reverse shells giving remote access to infected devices. GL.iNet manufactures networking equipment, including home and travel routers, as well as KVM devices that allow users to access and control computers remotely. Its GoodCloud platform allows customers to remotely manage supported devices, including accessing and controlling computers and servers connected to its KVM products. In a security advisory published on November 20, GL.iNet confirmed that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to access devices and install malicious software. "The attack path has been blocked. We fixed the cloud vulnerability and blocked the access used in this incident," the company said . "Devices can no longer be newly infected through this attack path. These measures do not remove malware from devices that were already infected." GL.iNet has not disclosed how the attackers exploited its cloud platform, how many customers were impacted, or whether information was stolen from compromised devices. The company is also investigating whether computers connected to infected KVM devices were compromised.
